rows.name: TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT

cells.Values and default: Whole number `0` or larger, digits only, parsed with `std::from_chars`. A value above `16` is lowered to `16`. Any other text, also empty text, aborts the process. Unset: 8 pieces. Empty: the value is invalid and the process aborts.
cells.Effect: Sets the largest number of pieces into which Tron splits the software attention work on one KV cache page (64 tokens). Different attention workers can then run the pieces. `0` or `1` turns splitting off. The attention worker count also limits the pieces. A minibatch of fewer than 32 tokens is not split. An invalid value passes startup. The first forward pass with software attention work then logs `invalid TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT` and aborts the process. No command-line option sets it. No log line shows the value.

rows.name: TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING

cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. A result above 0 forces head tiling on. Any other set value forces it off: `0`, a negative number, or text that is not a number. Unset: each FPGA card decides from its bitfile. Head tiling is on for project 01 or 03 at version 05.09 or later. Empty: forced off.
cells.Effect: Forces head tiling on or off for every FPGA card and skips the bitfile check. Head tiling applies when one hardware attention pass covers more KV cache tokens than a card handles for all heads. The card then gets one command that handles fewer heads per pass, not several commands. Words such as `true` force it off. A value above 0 turns head tiling on also for a bitfile that fails the check. No command-line option sets it. Check: when the variable is set, the log shows once `HW attention: TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING=<value> forces the feature ON` or `OFF`.

problems.statement: A negative number becomes a very large number.
problems.code_says: atol returns a signed long and the function returns size_t. `-1` becomes 2^64 - 1. std::min(max_main_helpers, n) then never lowers the helper count, so a negative number sets no upper limit.

cells.Values and default: Integer of 0 or more, parsed with `atol`. The unit is worker threads. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. A negative number converts to an unsigned 64-bit number. `-1` becomes 2^64 - 1 threads. That value sets no upper limit. Unset: half of the workers of the shared thread pool, rounded down. cells.Effect: Sets the largest number of main helpers in a forward pass, and `0` turns main helpers off. A value below `TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS` or its default aborts the process at model load. rows.name: TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH

cells.Values and default: Number without a unit, parsed with `std::atof`. It must be 0 or above. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. Unset: `0.1`. Empty: counts as `0`.
cells.Effect: Sets how strongly each update moves the speed estimate of each worker of the shared thread pool toward the mean of all workers. `0` removes this effect. The estimates split the attention work between the attention workers. At each update the mean of all workers gets the weight `1-exp(-value/timescale)`. The timescale is `TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE` or its default of 10 updates. A negative value aborts the process when the shared thread pool is created. The error line in the log names `prior_strength`. The estimates are not used with the option `--pay-for-determinism`.

rows.name: TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE

cells.Values and default: Number, parsed with `std::atof`. The unit is updates of the speed estimator. It must be above 0. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. Unset: `10` updates. Empty: counts as `0`, and the process aborts.
cells.Effect: Sets the time constant of the speed estimator of the shared thread pool. The estimator keeps a speed estimate for each worker. At each update, the estimator multiplies its stored measurements by `exp(-(1+p)/value)`, where `p` is `TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH`. A larger value makes the speed estimates change more slowly. The speed estimates split the attention work between the attention workers. A value of 0 or below aborts the process when the shared thread pool is created. The error line in the log names `timescale`. There is one update per forward pass. The estimates are not used with the option `--pay-for-determinism`.

rows.name: USE_HW_ATTN

cells.Values and default: Integer `N`, parsed with `atol`. `N` of `0` or less turns hardware attention off. `N` above `0` turns it on. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. Unset: on from token position 127 for models generated by ingest, off for other models. Empty: off for every model.
cells.Effect: Chooses hardware attention or software attention for every eligible model. `N` above `0` also sets the first token position that hardware attention serves. That position is the smallest value `k*128 - 1` that is not below `N`: `1` gives position 127, `128` gives position 255. No command-line option sets it. `true` and `on` count as `0` and turn it off. A model or server without hardware attention support stays on software attention. Check: the log lines `HW attention enabled for model` (field `engagement=`) and `HW attention disabled for model`.

problems.statement: A negative number becomes a very large limit.
problems.code_says: std::atoi returns a negative int and the constant is a size_t. `-1` becomes 2^64 - 1 levels. The depth is then limited only by the remaining token limit of the request and by the size limit.

cells.Values and default: Integer number of tree levels, parsed with `std::atoi`. The root counts as level 1. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. `0` and `1` draft no token. Unset: 2 levels. Empty: counts as `0`. No token is drafted then.
cells.Effect: Sets the largest depth of the draft tree. A draft step adds one level only while the tree has fewer levels than this value. With the default `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE` of 2 nodes, a depth above 2 levels adds no verified token. A negative number turns the depth limit off. No command-line option sets it. No log line shows the value.

notes: All 12 rows changed. No row contradicts the code. Five rows are imprecise. TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B: only model code that ingest generates reads the variable, and the hand-written plugin (h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp) never reads it. TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS, TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS, TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH: 'a very large number' gave no value and no outcome. TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH: the outcome of a negative number was missing, and the warning condition did not say that the defaults of 0 nodes and 2 levels trigger it. House-rule changes in the other rows: 'flag' became 'command-line option', and definitions of glossary terms (minibatch, main helper, attention worker, shared thread pool, speculative decoding, draft model, draft tree) were removed. Rule 7: the texts `Expected min_main_helpers <= max_main_helpers`, `Expected prior_strength >= 0.0f` and `Expected timescale > 0.0f` do appear in the log, but the source builds them from the format strings of TRON_ASSERT_LE, TRON_ASSERT_GE and TRON_ASSERT_GT (h/common/assert.hpp:82-87), so git grep -F does not find them. The four rows now say that the error line in the log names the identifier, which a reader can still search for. Rule 13: the Effect cell of TRON_HWATTN_COMPOUND_SPLIT now starts with the required sentence, and the sentence about a source comment is gone. 'Check:' was added to TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING (log line) and TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B (Perfetto event field min_b). The second one is a trace event, not a log line, a FUSE stats file or a command. Move it back to a plain sentence if 'Check:' must stay limited to those three. The two speedometer rows now name the option `--pay-for-determinism` (src/rinzler.cpp:4331, src/runtron.cpp:804) in place of the model config field. They also say when an invalid value aborts: when the shared thread pool is created (h/tron/threading.hpp:645), which is at model load at the latest (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1611). TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH: the three draft tree constants are namespace-scope statics, so the warning is logged at program start also without speculative decoding. TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE: the sentence that TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH is divided by the value was removed. The formula in the same cell already shows it, and the row was at 995 of 1,000 characters.
